summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell slightly to Rs 785 crore as curriculum-led Publication offtake slipped into Q2; FY27 Publication growth guided to ~10%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 785 crore, slightly lower YoY, with Publication down 3% to Rs 405 crore and Stationery up 2% to Rs 380 crore. Late release of state textbooks in Maharashtra and Gujarat pushed Publication sales into July (Q2), so management argues the shortfall is timing rather than loss. Export Stationery fell about 9% in the quarter and full-year export guidance was cut to around -5%, while Domestic Stationery grew 26%. Management guided Publication growth to about 10% for FY27, below the earlier ~15% expectation, and Stationery margin to about 8-10% amid brand investments and under-utilisation of a new polymer plant.

segments.name: Publication
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 405 crore (-3%) due to late state textbook release in Maharashtra and Gujarat; FY27 growth guided ~10% (earlier ~15%); margin guided 26-27% (later cited ~10% for year). Management said no MRP increase in FY27, so growth is all volume.

segments.name: Domestic Stationery
segments.commentary: Grew 26% in Q1 on brand association, new cover designs, and e-commerce and quick commerce; FY27 growth guided 15-17%. Brand spend and senior hiring for non-paper vertical pressured short-term profitability.

segments.name: Export Stationery
segments.commentary: Down about 9% in Q1 on US demand weakness, supply-chain and geopolitical disruption, and missed back-to-school orders; FY27 guidance cut to about -5% from high single-digit growth guided in May. New polymer plant ran at ~30% utilisation (Rs 65 crore investment), causing under-absorption.

segments.name: Indiannica
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 3 crore and PAT of Rs (-7) crore; seasonal business.

guidance_outlook: Publication FY27 revenue growth ~10% (management says 'more than 10%' possible); Q2 FY27 Publication revenue expected at Rs 130+ crore vs Rs 91 crore in Q2 FY26, i.e. ~Rs 45-50 crore additional YoY.
Domestic Stationery FY27 growth 15-17%; Export Stationery FY27 about -5%.
Stationery EBITDA margin around 8-10% for FY27 (Q1 margin commentary); 10-11% combined Stationery EBITDA margin cited as sustainable after brand investment phase.
Publication margin guided 26-27% (Q1 segment margin 40% per CFO); Q2 margin expected higher than Q1 but not better than Q1 in absolute terms, and much better YoY.
Polymer plant utilisation expected to normalise in FY27 per management, though timing depends on external factors.
Non-paper stationery targeted at 10-15% of Domestic Stationery in about 3 years; new categories to launch by end of calendar 2026.
capex_capacity: New polymer plant (investment ~Rs 65 crore) started in Q4 FY26, utilisation about 30%; intended mainly for exports, under-absorbed overheads hit Stationery margin.
Surplus cash from K-12 stake sale (Rs 330 crore, ~4.5% stake, leaving ~8.8%) to be held for organic and possible inorganic opportunities in Indian Stationery; no investment decision yet.
Supplementary books for Maharashtra and Gujarat curricula being launched for trade sale across grades up to 10 for CBSE schools.
demand_pricing: Maharashtra (grades 2, 3, 4, 6) and some Gujarat subjects changed in FY27; grades 2-6 are ~20% of Publication revenue, with ~50% growth expected in those grades. Gujarat next-year curriculum clarity not yet received.
Without curriculum change, Publication would have done Rs 30-35 crore in Q1 per management; spillover to Q2 expected.
Workbooks are ~45% of Publication revenue; schools recommend them, and private-school CBSE-type transitions reported growing 15%+ YoY.
Paper prices up ~Rs 2,000/ton since April; further hikes largely not implemented (~2% effective).

Export tariffs were absorbed by customers; management requested pass-back of refunds, with no positive response yet. US customers holding inventory, reorders weak due to US inflation; US share of exports has fallen from ~75% in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: How much Publication revenue is loss from curriculum delay and what will Q2 look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 30-35 crore would have been earned in Q1 without curriculum change; this shifts to Q2 plus curriculum-driven growth. Q2 Publication expected at Rs 130+ crore vs Rs 91 crore in Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 Publication growth outlook and does competition from coaching and EdTech content threaten it?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance ~10% for FY27 given Q1 uncertainty; management said more than 10% possible. Competition seen mainly in higher grades and is not comparable on price; primary-level changes limit that threat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Export Stationery guidance move from high single-digit growth to about -5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Gulf disruptions after May and US inflation hurt demand; back-to-school orders due before August did not arrive and cannot be recovered. Quantification of lost orders was not possible.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of Rs 330 crore from K-12 stake sale and will PE investments continue?
qa_highlights.answer: No investment thoughts currently; only strategic investments in education tech. Funds kept for organic and possible inorganic Stationery growth; the company does not want to be a financial investor.

qa_highlights.question: Polymer plant underutilisation and expected normalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant at about 30% utilisation; raw material prices rose and orders did not come; expected to normalise in FY27 but dependent on external factors.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic Stationery growth drivers and non-paper plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth driven by paper stationery, brand association, packaging and e-commerce/quick commerce; non-paper product refresh done, new categories by year-end, target 10-15% share in 3 years. Price/volume split not disclosed.

financial_highlights.change: management noted it is majority of business

risks_watch: Publication FY27 growth guidance of ~10% rests on Q2 catch-up; management has not yet confirmed Gujarat next-year curriculum changes, and Maharashtra/Gujarat timing has already slipped once.

Export Stationery guidance cut from high single-digit growth (May) to about -5%; US customers still holding inventory with weak reorders due to US inflation, and tariff refunds not yet passed back to Navneet.
Polymer plant at about 30% utilisation (Rs 65 crore investment) keeps under-absorption pressure on Stationery margin; normalisation in FY27 depends on external factors management does not control.
Stationery profitability under pressure from brand spend and senior hiring for non-paper vertical; sustainable combined Stationery EBITDA margin cited at 10-11%, versus 8-10% guided for FY27.
Q2 FY27 Publication revenue expected at Rs 130+ crore vs Rs 91 crore in Q2 FY26; management did not quantify Q2 EBITDA and analysts questioned the size of the expected Q2 uplift.
Use of Rs 330 crore K-12 stake sale proceeds undecided; management says no investment decisions yet, with possible inorganic Stationery opportunities.
key_quotes: So, overall, I can tell you that of the total Publication revenue, around 45 % comes from the workbook category.
And because Q1 is little nervous, I am giving guidance of 10%. But overall, if you ask me, we are quite positive about growing more than 10%.
So, overall, around Rs. 45 crores – Rs. 50 crores additional revenue should come compared to Q2’26.
And therefore, my new guidance of (-5%). We are very hopeful when first reduction in tariffs came in.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term Publication and domestic Stationery story but visibly cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly called the Q1 shortfall timing-driven and cut FY27 guidance (Publication ~10%, Export about -5%) after saying it was "nervous" about Q1. Evasive on quantification, declining to give price/volume splits for Stationery, the lost back-to-school export orders, or the Gujarat curriculum outlook.

adds.what: New polymer plant (~Rs 65 crore investment), mainly for exports, running at ~30% utilisation
Supplementary books for Maharashtra and Gujarat curricula for trade sale up to grade 10 (CBSE schools)

growth.why: FY27 Publication growth cut to ~10% (from ~15%) and Export Stationery to ~-5%, offset by Domestic Stationery guided at 15-17%; curriculum-driven Publication sales shifted into Q2 (Q2 guided Rs 130+ crore vs Rs 91 crore), but the new polymer plant runs at only ~30% utilisation.
